clue.text: Note, Pop's dancing with daughter on ice

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about, so the words note and pop's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical note and Dad's dancing with his daughter at an ice rink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on ice' looks like the skating rink but is the definition; 'dancing' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans put on ice are shelved for later, which is exactly what deferred means.

clue.text: Likeness to rap artist regularly is awkward

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy or ill-arranged, so the letters are rearranged
every other letter of artist is taken, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Comparing oneself to a rap artist is embarrassing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes R, I, T from artist; 'is awkward' rearranges them with TO RAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painted or photographed representation of a person, a likeness.

clue.text: Grave of dictator's endured

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone dictating aloud to a secretary, so this is how the word is pronounced

parts.note: stayed means lasted or endured

explanation.surface: The tomb of a tyrant has lasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dictator' suggests a tyrant, but means a person speaking words for someone to write down. 'Grave' looks like a tomb but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid means sober and serious in manner, as grave does.

clue.text: Beaten up prior to producing medley

indicators.note: beaten means battered or whisked, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone was assaulted before putting on a mixed show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten up' looks like a phrase, but 'Beaten' alone signals the rearrangement of UP PRIOR TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a mixture of dried petals, and by extension any miscellany or mixture.

clue.text: Sodium battery covers energy for part of aircraft

indicators.note: in a down clue, the battery word sits on top of the energy letter, covering it

parts.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
a cell is a single battery
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sodium battery wrapped round a power source, as an aircraft component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' looks like enclosing, but in a down answer the CELL simply sits above E.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacelle is the streamlined housing on an aircraft that holds an engine.

clue.text: Popular recording grabbing one, volume is turned up

indicators.note: in a down answer, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the recording letters hold the others inside them

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc recording
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tome is a large book or volume

explanation.surface: A record holding a single track gets its volume raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume is turned up' reads as louder, but 'turned up' reverses CITOMED, the CD holding I and TOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotic means of or for ordinary people, as popular can.

clue.text: Location around River Wear

indicators.note: the word for location goes around the river letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a spot is a location or place

explanation.surface: A place lies beside the River Wear, the river that flows through Durham in northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Wear' reads as the English river; split it: R is the river and 'Wear' is the definition, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport a hat or a beard is to wear it or show it off.

clue.text: Parody mostly is on right track

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, dropping its final letter

parts.note: a spoof is a parody or send-up

explanation.surface: A satire that mainly hits the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right track' reads as one phrase; 'on' places SPOO above R in this down answer, and 'track' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the trail of an animal, the tracks it leaves.

clue.text: Promise to include perhaps Milton Keynes's last regressive therapist

indicators.note: the promise word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: an oath is a solemn promise

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: John Milton, author of Paradise Lost, is an example of a poet

indicators.note: only the final letter of Keynes's is used

explanation.surface: A pledge to include the end of the new town of Milton Keynes in some backward plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton Keynes is an English new town; split it: Milton is the poet, and Keynes gives only its last letter. 'regressive' reverses POETS to STEOP.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats ailments by manipulating bones and muscles, a kind of therapist.

clue.text: Slavery unlikely to be found around Croatia

indicators.note: the unlikely word surrounds the country letters

parts.note: a tall story is an unlikely one
HR is the international vehicle registration code for Croatia, from Hrvatska

explanation.surface: Bondage is not expected to occur in the Balkan country.
explanation.walkthrough: TALL means unlikely, as in a tall tale; HR is Croatia's vehicle code.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrall means bondage or servitude, the condition of a slave.

clue.text: Central to Cairo, a strip joint

indicators.note: the letters needed sit in the centre of the run of words Cairo, a strip, spanning them

explanation.surface: A strip club in the middle of Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central to' signals letters found inside 'caiRO A STrip'; 'strip joint' wants to be one phrase, but 'joint' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of meat, such as beef cooked in the oven, is a roast.

clue.text: Dummy run follows company beginning to muster strength

indicators.note: the run letter is placed after everything else, following it
only the first letter of the word muster is used, its beginning

parts.note: a forte is someone's strong point or strength
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A practice exercise comes after a firm starts to gather its forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dummy run' reads as one phrase, but 'Dummy' alone is the definition, the British word for a baby's pacifier; 'follows' puts the run letter last.
explanation.definitionFit: A comforter is the British word for a baby's pacifier, also called a dummy.

clue.text: One that flies from socialist vote

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist
a poll is a vote or ballot

explanation.surface: Someone escaping a left-wing ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies from' suggests fleeing, but 'from' is only a link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A redpoll is a small finch, a bird, and so something that flies.

clue.text: Labour retains original manifesto, initially creating disquiet

indicators.note: the word for labour keeps the other letters held inside it

parts.note: toil is hard work or labour
the prefix ur- means original or primitive, as in Urtext

indicators.note: only the opening letter of manifesto is taken

explanation.surface: The Labour Party keeps its old manifesto, causing unease at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party, but means work here; UR is a borrowed German prefix meaning original.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of agitation and unrest, a strong form of disquiet.

clue.text: Extremely vulgar man cited some funny quotes

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the collected letters are put into a strange new order
only the extreme letters of vulgar, its first and last, are used

explanation.surface: A rather crude man quoted some amusing lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives VR from vulgar; 'funny' rearranges VR with MAN CITED SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Quotation marks are informally called quotes, the punctuation that encloses speech.

clue.text: Musician, 6, appearing with Solti in Brahms and Liszt

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six

indicators.note: Cockney rhyming slang for pissed, meaning drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A performer plays alongside conductor Georg Solti in works by the two composers.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference but is the Roman numeral VI. Brahms and Liszt is British rhyming slang for pissed, meaning drunk: it rearranges SOLTI IN into OLINIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist plays the violin, and so is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Machismo shown by island's housing policies

indicators.note: the island word holds the other word inside it, housing it

parts.note: the Isle of Man is the island, and the 's gives a final S
lines can be policies, as in the party line

explanation.surface: Swagger on display from an island's government plans.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island between Britain and Ireland; 'housing' puts the policies inside the island's name and its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is an assertive masculinity, which is a matter of virility and toughness.

clue.text: 3 is 27's cue to rob cast

indicators.note: cast can mean thrown about or reformed, so the letters are shaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A numbered signal prompts actors to commit a theft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like actors but rearranges CUE TO ROB.
explanation.definitionFit: Three multiplied by itself three times makes twenty-seven, so three is that number's third root.

clue.text: Patronising husband staggered I ran Hotel Grand

indicators.note: staggered means reeled about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars, is slang thou

explanation.surface: A condescending husband was amazed that the speaker ran the Grand Hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggered' looks like surprise but rearranges I RAN HOTEL; 'Hotel Grand' wants to be a name, but Grand is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sanctimonious or superior in manner is condescending, or patronising, to others.

clue.text: Upset Irish winter sportsman? That's more dangerous

indicators.note: in a down answer upset means turned over, so the Irish letters read bottom to top

parts.note: a skier is someone who takes part in a winter sport

explanation.surface: An Irish skier who has fallen is taking more chances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' suggests distress, but in a down answer it turns the Irish abbreviation upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Riskier means involving greater hazard, i.e. more perilous.

clue.text: Listen and learn, gaining knowledge

indicators.note: the learn word gains the knowledge word added to it

parts.note: to hear news is to learn of it
ken means range of knowledge, as in beyond one's ken

explanation.surface: Pay attention and study, picking up wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listen and learn' reads as one instruction, but 'Listen' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearken is an old-fashioned word for paying attention to sound, i.e. to listen.

clue.text: Prime minister loses case for state

indicators.note: the outer letters, the case around the name, are taken away

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a 19th-century British prime minister

explanation.surface: A premier is defeated in a lawsuit concerning a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses case' suggests a court defeat, but strips the outer D and I from DISRAELI.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a country in the Middle East, a nation state.

clue.text: Student's set back by small mistakes

indicators.note: set back means put in reverse, so the student word is read from end to start

parts.note: a pupil is a student, and the 's adds the plural ending
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A student is hampered by minor errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Student's' is read as pupil is, PUPILS, which 'set back' turns round before S.
explanation.definitionFit: Slip-ups are careless errors, small blunders.

clue.text: Unmarried German 14, say

indicators.note: M is the abbreviation for married, and un- here means take it out

parts.note: Anne-Sophie Mutter is a German violinist, the answer to 14 down

explanation.surface: A single German fiddler, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the example signal, but is the definition; 'Unmarried' removes M from MUTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter something is to speak it aloud or say it.

clue.text: Have I the skill to be friendly?

definitions.meaning: a question asking whether one is capable

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they are capable of being nice.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into three words, AM I ABLE, to get the question; 'to be' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: An amiable person is genial and good-natured, which is what friendly means.

clue.text: Noble's heading for birthday party

indicators.note: the heading of birthday is its first letter

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is going to a birthday celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble' looks like an aristocrat, but is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Brave and noble both describe courageous, admirable conduct.

clue.text: Not very smart? That's rather unfair

definitions.meaning: a phrase of mild complaint, meaning that is somewhat unreasonable

explanation.surface: Calling someone dim is somewhat unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British idioms: 'thick' means stupid, and 'a bit thick' also means unreasonable or excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom serves both: mildly stupid, and also an informal British complaint that something goes too far.

clue.text: Earl introduces artist to one inspiring poet?

indicators.note: the earl letter comes first, introducing what follows

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A nobleman presents a painter to a poet's muse.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is a crossword convention for an artist; 'to' is a piece, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry in Greek myth, so she inspires poets.

clue.text: Subsequent change, reversing Article 50

indicators.note: the pair of letters for article and fifty are turned round in place

parts.note: to alter is to change
A is the indefinite article and L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A later change reverses the Brexit process under Article 50 of the EU treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: Article 50 is the EU treaty clause the UK triggered to leave the EU; here it simply gives A and L, which 'reversing' swaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Something subsequent comes afterwards in time.

clue.text: Born again Christian finally given rise after religious teaching

indicators.note: the other pieces come after the religious teaching letters

parts.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject

indicators.note: only the last letter of Christian is used

parts.note: an ascent is a rise or climb

explanation.surface: A born-again Christian gets a lift after religious instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Born again Christian' reads as one phrase; 'Born again' is the definition and Christian only gives N. RE is Religious Education, a school subject in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent describes something being reborn or revived, coming back to life.
